rationale: A wins because it keeps the story where the facts can hold weight and tells the founder which missing proof will make or break the pitch. Its line "the most newsworthy fact is what is NOT yet known (the post-relaunch paying-user trend)" is exactly the discipline this update needs. B has useful shapes, but "AI matchmaking just went mainstream" turns one company relaunch into a category proclamation the facts do not support. That is how a decent angle gets a reporter to ask for the receipt you do not have.
gaps_in_A: "Dating apps add AI to write your opening line — and some users hate it" stretches the supplied fact. We have Bumble adding AI and some users criticizing AI in dating as inauthentic; we do not have plural dating apps or direct evidence that users "hate" this Bumble feature.

"Bumble keeps women-message-first as it hands message-writing to AI" is a good tension, but "hands message-writing to AI" overstates "helps users write opening messages." The set does flag the missing mechanic, but the headline still outruns the fact.
"Dorsey/Schultz/Kalanick-adjacent storyline" is a little too inside-baseball and risks making the pitch sound templated. The founder-return frame works without dragging in famous-comeback shorthand.
gaps_in_B: "her first fix is AI" and "the first concrete strategic move since her return" are invented. The update says the relaunch is happening under the returning founder-CEO, not that it is her first move or her declared fix.
"analysts and investors are actively evaluating the thesis" is unsupported. You can say investors will want proof; you cannot conjure active analyst reaction from thin air.
"AI matchmaking just went mainstream" and "category-standard feature" are deck-slide claims, not reported facts. One Bumble relaunch is a data point, not a category shift.

"Bumble's brand promise is that its message-first model empowers authentic connection" adds brand language the update did not give you, then uses it to heighten the contradiction. The real tension is women-message-first versus AI-assisted opening messages; do not garnish it.
